ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Consider a thin rigid wire-frame MNPP'N'M' in which MNN'M' and NPP'N' are two squares of side $L$ with resistance per unit-length $\lambda$ and their planes are perpendicular. The frame is rotated with a constant angular velocity $\omega$ around an axis passing through $\mathrm{NN}$ ' and put in a region with constant magnetic field $B$ pointing perpendicular to $\mathrm{NN}^{\prime}$. What is the total heat released on the frame per revolution (in Joules)? Use $L=1 \mathrm{~m}, \lambda=1 \Omega / \mathrm{m}, \omega=2 \pi \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$ and $B=1 \mathrm{~T}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the black wireframe forms a bent closed hexagonal conducting wire M-N-P-P'-N'-M'-M. On the right is the square NPP'N', and on the left is the square MNN'M' in a plane perpendicular to it. The green dashed line passes through N and N', marked with angular velocity ω, indicating the rotation axis; it is not part of the black conducting wire. The red arrow B indicates the direction of the magnetic field, and is perpendicular to the NN' axis. Reasoning: According to the actual closed path of the conducting wire in the figure, the total length of the conducting wire is 6L, so the total resistance R = 6λL. The two mutually perpendicular square faces can be regarded as folded cross-faces of the same closed loop. Let the phase of the angle between the area normal of one square and the magnetic field be θ = ωt; the other, because the plane is perpendicular, differs by π/2. Then the total magnetic flux can be written as Φ = B L^2(cos θ + sin θ), and the overall sign does not affect the heat. By Faraday's law, the induced electromotive force ε = -dΦ/dt = B L^2 ω(sin θ - cos θ) (differing by an overall sign does not affect the square). The instantaneous power P = ε^2/R. Over one period, the average value of (sin θ - cos θ)^2 is 1, so the average power is (B L^2 ω)^2/(6λL). The time for one revolution is T = 2π/ω, so the heat Q = [(B L^2 ω)^2/(6λL)](2π/ω). Substituting L=1 m, λ=1 Ω/m, B=1 T, ω=2π rad/s, gives Q = (4π^2/6) = 2π^2/3 ≈ 6.58 J.

raw_record.question_text: Consider a thin rigid wire-frame MNPP'N'M' in which MNN'M' and NPP'N' are two squares of side $L$ with resistance per unit length $\lambda$, and their planes are perpendicular. The frame is rotated with a constant angular velocity $\omega$ around an axis passing through $\mathrm{NN}'$ and placed in a region with constant magnetic field $B$ pointing perpendicular to $\mathrm{NN}'$. What is the total heat released on the frame per revolution (in Joules)? Use $L=1\ \mathrm{m}$, $\lambda=1\ \Omega/\mathrm{m}$, $\omega=2\pi\ \mathrm{rad}/\mathrm{s}$, and $B=1\ \mathrm{T}$.

method.method_draft: Flux/Faraday route. First read the image as a single bent hexagonal conducting wire M-N-P-P'-N'-M'-M: the green dashed line through N and N' is the rotation axis, not a black conducting side, so the total wire length is 6L and the resistance is R = 6λL. The two square panels are perpendicular and can be used as a folded spanning surface for the one closed loop. Let the two square area normals have phases θ and θ + π/2 relative to the fixed magnetic field B, with θ = ωt. The total magnetic flux through the folded surface is the sum of the two square fluxes, e.g. Φ = B L^2(cos θ + sin θ) up to sign convention. Faraday's law gives emf ε = -dΦ/dt = B L^2 ω(sin θ - cos θ) up to sign. The heat rate is P = ε^2/R. Average ε^2 over one full revolution: average of (sin θ - cos θ)^2 is 1. Thus Q = [(B L^2 ω)^2/(6λL)](2π/ω). Substitute L=1, λ=1, B=1, ω=2π to get Q = 2π^2/3 ≈ 6.58 J.

method.method_draft: Motional-emf line-integral route. From the image, take NN' as the vertical rotation axis and the wire as the outer six-sided loop M-N-P-P'-N'-M'-M. Therefore R = 6λL. Set the rotation axis as z and B along a fixed horizontal x direction. Let the radial direction to the M-side square be e1 = (cos θ, sin θ, 0), and the radial direction to the P-side square be e2 = (-sin θ, cos θ, 0), because the two square planes are perpendicular. For a point at radius r from the axis, v = ω zhat × r, so v × B is parallel to the axis. Hence the four radial/top-bottom connecting segments contribute zero to ∮(v × B)·dl; only the two outer vertical segments MM' and PP' contribute. Around the loop, their contributions combine as ε = ω B L^2[(e2·xhat) - (e1·xhat)] = -ω B L^2(sin θ + cos θ), up to orientation. Then P(t)=ε^2/(6λL). Since the average of (sin θ + cos θ)^2 over a revolution is 1, Q = [(ω B L^2)^2/(6λL)](2π/ω). With L=λ=B=1 and ω=2π, Q = 2π^2/3 ≈ 6.58 J.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：两张附图显示同一刚性线框结构：绿色虚线竖直穿过 N 和 N'，表示转轴 NN'；绿色弯箭头标出绕该竖直轴的角速度 ω；红色箭头 B 水平指向左方，因此磁场垂直于 NN'。黑色导线形成外部六边形闭合回路 M-N-P-P'-N'-M'-M，其中 MNN'M' 与 NPP'N' 两个正方形面相互垂直。推理：按指定方法取导线总长度为 6L，所以总电阻 R = 6λL。设转轴 NN' 为 z 轴，磁场沿固定水平 x 方向。令 M 侧正方形的径向单位矢量 e1 = (cosθ, sinθ, 0)，P 侧正方形的径向单位矢量 e2 = (-sinθ, cosθ, 0)，两者相差 90°。对离转轴半径为 r 的点，速度 v = ω zhat × r，因此 v × B 沿 z 轴方向。于是水平或径向边上的 dl 与 v × B 垂直，不贡献动生电动势；只有外侧两条竖直边 MM' 和 PP' 有贡献。沿回路 M-N-P-P'-N'-M'-M 积分得 ε = ω B L^2[(e2·xhat) - (e1·xhat)] = -ω B L^2(sinθ + cosθ)，符号不影响热量。瞬时焦耳功率 P(t)=ε^2/R = [ω^2 B^2 L^4(sinθ+cosθ)^2]/(6λL)。一周内 <(sinθ+cosθ)^2> = 1，周期 T = 2π/ω，所以每转放热 Q = [(ω B L^2)^2/(6λL)](2π/ω)。代入 L=1 m, λ=1 Ω/m, B=1 T, ω=2π rad/s：Q = (2π)^2/(6) = 2π^2/3 ≈ 6.58 J。

raw_record.original_question: Consider a thin rigid wire-frame MNPP'N'M' in which MNN'M' and NPP'N' are two squares of side $L$ with resistance per unit length $\lambda$, and their planes are perpendicular. The frame is rotated with a constant angular velocity $\omega$ around an axis passing through $\mathrm{NN}'$ and placed in a region with constant magnetic field $B$ pointing perpendicular to $\mathrm{NN}'$. What is the total heat released on the frame per revolution (in Joules)? Use $L=1\ \mathrm{m}$, $\lambda=1\ \Omega/\mathrm{m}$, $\omega=2\pi\ \mathrm{rad}/\mathrm{s}$, and $B=1\ \mathrm{T}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the black wireframe forms a bent closed hexagonal conducting wire M-N-P-P'-N'-M'-M. On the right is the square NPP'N', and on the left is the square MNN'M' in a plane perpendicular to it. The green dashed line passes through N and N', marked with angular velocity ω, indicating the rotation axis; it is not part of the black conducting wire. The red arrow B indicates the direction of the magnetic field, and is perpendicular to the NN' axis.

Reasoning: According to the actual closed path of the conducting wire in the figure, the total length of the conducting wire is 6L, so the total resistance R = 6λL. The two mutually perpendicular square faces can be regarded as folded cross-faces of the same closed loop. Let the phase of the angle between the area normal of one square and the magnetic field be θ = ωt; the other, because the plane is perpendicular, differs by π/2. Then the total magnetic flux can be written as Φ = B L^2(cos θ + sin θ), and the overall sign does not affect the heat. By Faraday's law, the induced electromotive force ε = -dΦ/dt = B L^2 ω(sin θ - cos θ) (differing by an overall sign does not affect the square). The instantaneous power P = ε^2/R. Over one period, the average value of (sin θ - cos θ)^2 is 1, so the average power is (B L^2 ω)^2/(6λL). The time for one revolution is T = 2π/ω, so the heat Q = [(B L^2 ω)^2/(6λL)](2π/ω). Substituting L=1 m, λ=1 Ω/m, B=1 T, ω=2π rad/s, gives Q = (4π^2/6) = 2π^2/3 ≈ 6.58 J.
